statements.text: Goff defends a form in which micro-(proto)phenomenal facts and macro phenomenal facts are both fundamental, so the relation between them is intelligible causation rather than constitution. It treats the macro-physical as nothing over and above the macro-phenomenal, which removes causal competition at the level of brains, though it would struggle if the micro level is causally closed.

sources.quote: intelligible emergentist Russellian monism, which remains attractive despite not possessing all the virtues Chalmers attributes to the constitutive view
the emergentist Russellian monist takes the macro-physical to be nothing over and above the macro-phenomenal
